title: Studying English and taking exams
subtitle: fluent, accurate, pass an exam
summary: Describe how well someone speaks English and talk about revising for exams and passing them.

lesson.heading: Vocabulary, accuracy and fluency
lesson.text: Nastya is an English teacher. She says Jade has a **wide vocabulary** and speaks very **accurately**, but she needs to practise more to become **fluent**.

examples.text: Jade has a **wide vocabulary**.
examples.note: = she knows a lot of words

examples.text: She speaks very **accurately**.
Elke is quite **fluent**.
examples.note: = able to speak naturally without stopping

examples.text: Jose's vocabulary is quite **basic**, so he needs to **increase** it.
examples.note: basic = elementary, simple; increase = make it bigger

lesson.heading: Accent, vowels and consonants
lesson.text: Your **accent** is the way you pronounce words. The letters a, e, i, o and u are the **vowels**; all the other letters of the **alphabet** are **consonants**.

examples.text: His **accent** isn't very good; in particular he has problems with certain **consonants**.
There are twenty-six letters in the **alphabet**.
Jose has no problem **making himself understood**.
examples.note: = saying things in a way people understand

lesson.heading: Making progress
lesson.text: Olga is always **willing to experiment with language**, so she sometimes **gets things wrong**, but she learns from her mistakes and is **making a lot of progress**. Andreas **picks things up** very quickly and has **a good ear for language**.

examples.text: She is **willing to** try new words.
She sometimes **gets things wrong**.
He **picks** new words **up** very quickly.
He has **a good ear for language**.
examples.note: = he is good at hearing and repeating sounds and words

lesson.heading: Adjective or adverb?
lesson.note: Not a fluently speaker, not she speaks accurate, and not I speak English good.

lesson.heading: Exams: the verbs
lesson.text: You **take** or **do** an exam - never *make* an exam. Before the exam you **revise for** it. If you are successful and **do well**, you **pass**; if you do badly, you **fail**. Sometimes you can **retake** an exam, that is, do it again.

examples.text: Tomas wants to **take** the exam in June.
I have to **revise for** my exam next week.
I'm sure she'll **pass** the exam.
Karin **failed** the exam, but she can **retake** it next year.

lesson.heading: Around the exam
lesson.text: A **candidate** is someone taking an exam. If you do well you get a good **grade** (or **mark**). Preparing is **hard work**, but you **do your best**, do some **revision** and some **exam preparation**, and **work on** the things you find difficult.

examples.text: There are over 100 **candidates** taking the exam.
A+ is the highest **grade** you can get.
He's **doing his best**.
I'm trying to **get through** the coursebook.
I want the students to write an **essay**.
examples.note: an essay = a short piece of writing on one subject

lesson.text: The verb is **revise**, the noun is **revision**: *I must revise tonight* = *I must do some revision tonight*.

exercises.prompt: My sister picks ___ languages very quickly.
exercises.explanation: Pick something up = learn it without really trying.

exercises.prompt: I will have to revise ___ my exam next week.

exercises.explanation: Do your best = make as much effort as you can. You can also say try your best.

exercises.prompt: Karin ___ the exam, but she can retake it next year.
exercises.explanation: You pass an exam if you are successful and fail it if you are not.

exercises.prompt: A+ is the highest ___ you can get.
exercises.explanation: Grade and mark both mean the result you get in an exam.

exercises.prompt: There are over 100 ___ taking the exam.
exercises.explanation: A candidate is someone who is taking an exam.

exercises.prompt: We had to write an ___ for homework in not more than 200 words.
exercises.explanation: An essay is a short piece of writing about a particular subject.

exercises.prompt: I need to ___ my vocabulary; it's still very basic.
exercises.explanation: Increase your vocabulary = learn more words.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Does Victor know a lot of English? *B:* No, but he can make himself ___.
exercises.explanation: Make yourself understood = say things in a way people understand.

exercises.prompt: Is the letter a vowel or a consonant?
Match each word with its meaning.
Say that you are good at hearing and repeating new sounds.
exercises.answer: I have a good ear for language.
exercises.explanation: A good ear for language = you are good at hearing, repeating and understanding sounds and words.

exercises.statement: Andreas is a fluently speaker with a very wide vocabulary.
exercises.explanation: Andreas is a fluent speaker with a very wide vocabulary. Use the adjective fluent with a noun, and the adverb fluently with a verb.
